matched.actualTitle: JWT Secret Exposure in Docker Environment - Privilege Escalation
matched.matchReason: Both findings identify exposure of sensitive configuration including JWT_SECRET and MIGRATION_SECRET through the admin config export endpoint. The actual finding encompasses this vulnerability as a component of a broader privilege escalation attack leveraging the exposed JWT secret.

matched.actualTitle: NoSQL Injection via Object Injection in Email and Password Fields
matched.matchReason: Both findings identify object injection vulnerabilities where unserialized data containing operator objects (comparable to PHP gadgets) cause crashes and potential command execution. The actual finding demonstrates the same vulnerability principle applied to MongoDB operators via JSON object injection.

matched.actualTitle: Exposed Environment Configuration Files Containing Multiple API Credentials and Secrets
matched.matchReason: Both findings deal with exposure of sensitive application secrets and credentials. The actual finding of exposed .env files is semantically aligned with the expected backup file disclosure vulnerability, as both result in credential exposure through improperly secured files.

missed.title: PHP Object Injection via Memcached
missed.reason: While NoSQL/object injection vulnerabilities were discovered, no specific evidence was found demonstrating PHP unserialize() gadget chains (SqlExecutor) executing arbitrary SQL in __wakeup() method on Memcached session data. The actual findings show MongoDB operator crashes rather than PHP object serialization exploitation.

missed.title: Cross-System Privilege Escalation via Shared Database
missed.reason: No evidence was found of legacy and modern systems sharing a MySQL user table or an admin user injected via legacy system being trusted by the modern API. This specific cross-system privilege escalation scenario was not identified in the actual findings.

extra.title: JWT Secret Exposure in Docker Environment - Privilege Escalation
extra.assessment: New discovery - This is a critical finding that extends beyond the expected findings. The exposure of JWT_SECRET (m0d3rn_jwt_s3cr3t_k3y_2025) in Docker environment variables enables privilege escalation attacks through token forgery, which is more severe than just configuration exposure.

extra.title: Information Disclosure: JWT Claims Exposed in Response Body
extra.assessment: New discovery - Redundant exposure of JWT claims (iat, exp) in response body allows fingerprinting of token generation patterns. While low severity, this is a genuine security issue not in expected findings.

extra.title: Critical CSRF Vulnerability: Static OAuth2 State Parameter
extra.assessment: New discovery - The use of static, non-unique state parameter (eyJyZXR1cm5QYXRobmFtZSI6Ii8ifQ%3D%3D) completely undermines OAuth2 CSRF protection mechanisms and enables account takeover attacks.

extra.title: User Enumeration via Login Endpoint Timing Side-Channel
extra.assessment: New discovery - Timing differential (~20x) between valid and invalid user emails (58-62ms vs 2-3ms) enables user enumeration. This is a valid security finding not in the expected list.

extra.title: Missing Critical Security Response Headers
extra.assessment: New discovery - Absence of security headers (X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, X-XSS-Protection, HSTS, CSP, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy) leaves application vulnerable to MIME-sniffing, clickjacking, and XSS attacks in older browsers.

extra.title: Weak Password Validation - No Complexity Requirements
extra.assessment: New discovery - Registration accepts passwords as short as 3 characters, numeric-only passwords, and dictionary words without enforcing any complexity requirements. This enables weak credential creation.

extra.title: Account Takeover via Duplicate Email Registration (No Uniqueness Constraint)
extra.assessment: New discovery - The registration endpoint allows re-registering the same email with different passwords without enforcing email uniqueness constraints, enabling account takeover attacks.

extra.title: Missing Rate Limiting on Login Endpoint - Brute Force Attack
extra.assessment: New discovery - Complete absence of rate limiting allows rapid brute force and credential stuffing attacks. 21 password combinations tested against a single account in 1-2 seconds without throttling.

extra.title: NoSQL Injection via Object Type Confusion in Login and Registration Endpoints
extra.assessment: New discovery - Insufficient input validation allows MongoDB operators ($ne, $gt, $regex, $exists) to be passed as objects, causing crashes and potential authentication bypass. Related to but distinct from the expected object injection finding.

extra.title: Insufficient Email Validation - Invalid Email Formats Accepted
extra.assessment: New discovery - Registration accepts invalid email formats (missing @, incomplete domains, localhost, etc.) without RFC 5322 validation. This enables registration with non-deliverable addresses.

extra.title: Minimal Service Response - No Valid Endpoints Discovered
extra.assessment: New discovery - The service at localhost:13557 appears to be a placeholder or misconfigured HTTP server returning 404 for all paths. May be a honeypot or intentionally minimal test service.

extra.title: Information Disclosure - Endpoint Listing via Root Endpoint
extra.assessment: New discovery - The root endpoint returns JSON listing all API endpoints including protected admin endpoints, facilitating API reconnaissance attacks.

extra.title: JWT Algorithm Confusion Vulnerability (HS256 vs RS256)
extra.assessment: New discovery - The JWT middleware explicitly accepts both RS256 and HS256 algorithms, creating an algorithm confusion vulnerability that enables token forgery by signing with HS256 using the public key.

extra.title: Missing Rate Limiting on Authentication Endpoints
extra.assessment: New discovery - No rate limiting on auth endpoints enables brute force, user enumeration, credential stuffing, and account takeover attacks. Multiple successful rapid requests confirmed.

extra.title: Cross-Site WebSocket Hijacking (CSWSH) - No Origin Header Validation
extra.assessment: New discovery - WebSocket server accepts connections with arbitrary or missing Origin headers, enabling CSWSH attacks where attacker JavaScript can execute RPC calls with victim's privileges.

extra.title: No Rate Limiting on User Registration (Batch Account Creation)
extra.assessment: New discovery - Complete absence of rate limiting on registration allows creation of 10+ accounts in less than 1 second (~84ms per account) without CAPTCHA or verification, enabling batch account creation attacks.
